views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our current retaliatory posture but signal readiness to negotiate at the G20 meeting agreed in the Nov 1 Trump-Xi call, with the concrete goal of freezing the threatened Jan 1 escalation of List 3 from 10% to 25%. Offer incremental US import purchases as a face-saving path to a truce, but make no structural concessions on IP/tech-transfer before talks bear fruit. Do not escalate further, as escalation risks drawing US coverage of all Chinese exports onto a broader battlefield at a moment our currency and reserves are already under pressure.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high but not existential. By decision date the US had already locked in ~$250B of tariffs on Chinese goods (List 1+2 at 25%, List 3 at 10% since Sept 24) with List 3 scheduled to jump to 25% on Jan 1, and Trump has threatened to extend tariffs to effectively all Chinese exports (~$500B+). That is a direct, material hit to the export economy. Simultaneously the yuan has lost ~9-10% versus the dollar and is pressing toward the 7.0 level, FX reserves fell a record ~$34B in October to an 18-month low of ~$3.05T, and the PBOC was forced to act (hiking the short-yuan reserve requirement to 20% and cutting bank reserve ratios to support a slowing economy). Offsetting these, China's exports remained surprisingly resilient in the short run — September exports rose ~15% y/y — but that strength is sustained by order front-loading ahead of the January hike and is not durable; the economy is still growing near its ~6.5% target with ample reserves, and Beijing retains policy levers (retaliation, easing, trade diversification). This lands between the +0.5 'high' anchor and the existential threshold. On action: with a leaders' meeting at the G20 now agreed, the rational move is to negotiate rather than escalate — escalation would legitimize a US move to blanket coverage and the 25% rate at a time of FX and reserve strain. De-escalation to full concession is premature, since talks are not yet advanced and there is no matching US offer; 'negotiate' — maintain posture, seek a freeze on the Jan 1 hike via purchases — is the calibrated stance.

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5-10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
Trump and Xi hold a phone call focused on trade; agree to meet at the G20 in Argentina.

China's foreign exchange reserves fell more than expected to an 18-month low in October... Reserves fell by $33.93 billion in October to $3.053 trillion... biggest monthly decline since December 2016... yuan slipped closer to the psychologically important level of 7 per dollar.
Chinese exports rose nearly 15% in September... US tariffs set to become more punishing... resilience of exports is unlikely to be sustained.
Trump and Xi agreed to meet... The two leaders had a call on Thursday, officially agreeing to meet in Argentina and laying the ground for further discussions on trade.
